model_priors.model_reasoning: TFRC (Transferrin Receptor 1, CD71) is the canonical textbook example of a constitutively and rapidly internalizing cell-surface receptor. It cycles between the plasma membrane and endosomes continuously via clathrin-mediated endocytosis, driven by a well-characterized YTRF tyrosine-based internalization motif (Y20 in the cytoplasmic tail, fitting the YXX[hydrophobic] consensus) as well as a dileucine-like element. The receptor internalizes with a half-life on the cell surface of ~5–10 minutes, making it one of the fastest-internalizing receptors known. The topology confirms a type II single-pass transmembrane protein with a short N-terminal cytoplasmic tail (~65 aa) containing these motifs, and a large extracellular domain. There is no ambiguity here — this is the prototypical high-internalizing receptor used as a positive control in trafficking studies.

per_isoform.topology_summary: Type II single-pass TM protein; N-terminus cytoplasmic (~65 aa), C-terminus extracellular (~674 aa); 1 TM helix.
per_isoform.endocytic_motifs_noted: YTRF at positions ~19-22 (YXX[hydrophobic] tyrosine-based internalization motif, cytoplasmic tail); also a dileucine-like element in the cytoplasmic tail. Both reside in the confirmed cytoplasmic N-terminal region.
per_isoform.rationale: TFRC is the archetypal constitutively internalizing receptor. The cytoplasmic tail contains the canonical YTRF motif (Y20) that directly engages AP-2 clathrin adaptor for rapid, clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Surface half-life is ~5–10 minutes; the receptor continuously cycles between plasma membrane and recycling endosomes. This is one of the best-characterized high-internalization proteins in cell biology, used routinely as a positive control for endocytosis assays. Confidence is maximal.

basal.rationale: Multiple independent sources confirm TfR1 undergoes strong constitutive (basal) internalization via clathrin-mediated endocytosis driven by its cytoplasmic YTRF motif interacting with AP2/mu2. It is explicitly described as a model protein for 'well-characterized, strong constitutive internalization via CME.' The PKCbetaII/AAK1/AP2M1 axis further regulates this basal clathrin recruitment. TfR1 is also used as a benchmark for constitutive endocytosis in TransTAC and LYTAC platforms.

native_ligand.rationale: Holo-transferrin (iron-laden Tf) drives robust clathrin-mediated endocytosis of TfR1 across multiple cell types including hepatocytes, brain endothelial cells, erythroid cells, and HL-60 cells. After endosomal iron release, the receptor-apotransferrin complex recycles to the surface for further rounds. This is the canonical, well-established internalization route.

therapeutic.rationale: Multiple therapeutic modalities targeting TfR1 show efficient internalization: anti-TfR1 antibody T8IgG1 internalizes efficiently into tumor cells; VHH-Fc constructs internalize into CHO and brain endothelial cells; anti-CD71 ADC INA03 rapidly internalizes into lysosomal compartments of leukemic cells; TransTACs drive rapid co-internalization; HFn-based LYTACs exploit TfR1-mediated lysosomal endocytosis; CD71-targeting aptamers internalize into pancreatic cancer cells. Flow cytometry modeling of anti-TfR antibody internalization in B-cell lymphoblastoid lines further quantifies this.

literature.rationale: TFRC (TfR1/CD71) is one of the most extensively characterized internalizing receptors in the literature. All three modes—basal constitutive, native ligand (transferrin)-driven, and therapeutic (antibody/ADC/aptamer/engineered ligand)-driven—are graded high with high confidence. The receptor constitutively cycles via clathrin-mediated endocytosis through its YTRF motif, is dramatically upregulated on tumor cells, and efficiently internalizes a wide variety of exogenous binders into endosomal/lysosomal compartments. It is explicitly used as a benchmark model for strong constitutive CME and is actively exploited for drug delivery, ADC payloads, and targeted protein degradation platforms.
literature.cross_condition_note: Brain endothelial cells show markedly lower general endocytic rates than peripheral endothelial cells despite sharing TfR1, suggesting cell-type context modulates internalization efficiency. Therapeutic binders (ADC INA03, TransTACs, VHH-Fc) show rapid lysosomal routing in tumor/leukemic cells, while the native transferrin cycle is predominantly a recycling pathway rather than a degradative one.

source.title: Targeting Transferrin Receptor 1 for Enhancing Drug Delivery Through the Blood-Brain Barrier for Alzheimer's Disease

spans.quote: Drug delivery to the brain faces a critical obstacle in the form of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which severely limits therapeutic options for Alzheimer's disease (AD). Transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) is abundantly expressed in brain capillary endothelial cells, offering a potential pathway for circumventing this barrier. Physiologically, TfR1 binds to iron-laden transferrin, leading to cellular uptake through clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Within acidic endosomes, the iron is released, and the receptor-apotransferrin complex recycles to the cell surface for further rounds of transport.

source.title: Transferrin receptor 1 binds human parvovirus B19 VP1u to facilitate entry

spans.quote: Human parvovirus B19 (B19V) displays a strict tropism for erythroid progenitor cells, which is governed by the VP1 unique domain (VP1u). This domain mediates cell-specific uptake through interaction with an unknown cellular receptor, termed VP1uR. Proximity labeling in permissive erythroid cells identifies transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1/CD71) as a predominant membrane protein associated with VP1u. VP1u constructs colocalize with TfR1 at the cell surface of erythroid cells. Incubation with anti-TfR1 antibody OKT9 abolishes binding and uptake of recombinant VP1u.

sources.claim: OKT9 anti-TfR1 antibody efficiently inhibits B19V uptake and infection, confirming TfR1 is required for viral uptake into erythroid cells.

source.title: Transferrin receptor 1 binds human parvovirus B19 VP1u to facilitate entry

spans.quote: While OKT9 efficiently inhibits B19V uptake and infection, it does not block virus binding to host cells. Direct binding assays confirm interaction of VP1u with human TfR1. Using cryo-EM we solved the 2.4 Å structure of the TfR1-VP1u complex, mapping the binding site. These findings establish TfR1 as the previously unknown receptor, VP1uR, required for B19V uptake.

spans.quote: Lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) hold therapeutic potential by degrading pathogenesis-associated proteins. However, current LYTAC systems often require considerable effort for case-by-case construction and are devoid of a convenient and efficient modular platform. Here, we develop a modular LYTAC platform based on human heavy chain ferritin (HFn), leveraging its peptide-display function and TfR1-mediated lysosomal endocytosis. This system comprises a bioengineered HFn scaffold with enhanced TfR1 affinity and target-specific affibodies conjugated to the HFn via SpyTag-SpyCatcher system.
